subject.title: Bug: isRecurringTopOfHourCronExpr fails to match cron expressions with step values

question: Should OpenClaw broaden the automatic top-of-hour stagger default to cron minute fields that include zero, even though current docs describe literal minute `0` and existing sub-hourly schedules would start inheriting a 5-minute offset?
rationale: The source confirms the current limitation, but the requested behavior changes default scheduling semantics for existing users and conflicts with the current public docs wording.

options.title: Broaden with compatibility proof
options.body: Update the detector, docs, and regression tests so minute fields that include zero get the default stagger while explicit exact schedules remain exact.

options.title: Keep literal-minute contract
options.body: Treat the current docs as the product contract and close this issue after explaining that sub-hourly schedules need explicit `--stagger` today.

options.title: Pause on the fork PR
options.body: Leave this issue open while maintainers decide whether to adopt or replace the uneditable fork PR before starting any new repair lane.

recommendation.title: Broaden with compatibility proof
recommendation.body: Update the detector, docs, and regression tests so minute fields that include zero get the default stagger while explicit exact schedules remain exact.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced the default stagger behavior and has the strongest observed history in the cron scheduling area.
